matches.rationale: No report finding covers MIN_DEPOSIT rent calculation or the missing 128-byte storage overhead.
Finding 4 says the bump comes in as an argument and is stored unvalidated in deposit/withdraw, and recommends using ctx.bumps.
Finding 12 is about an unused chainId parameter. Finding 14 is about the return value. Neither says the emitted destination chain id is wrong (Ethereum instead of Eclipse).
No finding covers msg! log truncation in log_outbox_message.
Finding 3 is about the nonce being predictable through weak randomness. It does not raise the 64-bit width or the missing check that a nonce was already used in sendNonces.
No finding covers the addressArrayInitialized modifier accepting an empty array.
Finding 2 says transfers come from the relayer account rather than a program-controlled PDA, a centralization risk, and recommends PDA control of funds. That is the relayer custody design concern.
No finding covers missing _disableInitializers in the implementation constructors.
Finding 2, the only one that mentions invoke_signed, is already matched to the custody concern, and it argues for adding seeds rather than saying plain invoke is enough.
Finding 11 identifies the hardcoded 1024-byte sizes in WithdrawalReceipt::size and Configuration::size as wasting rent.
